thread:
maya: Heads-up — PR #4825 is ready for review. I added a streaming JSON schema example and updated the SDK snippets (Python + TS). Need eyes on accuracy + link targets before merge.

jon: Nice. pinging @rachel for SDK changes. Are we replacing the old 'tools' example or keeping it as a compatibility note?

maya: Replacing. This follows the "functions" shape in the latest runtime API. I left a short migration blurb. Example included inline: ```json
{
  "name": "get_weather",
  "parameters": {
    "type": "object",
    "properties": {
      "location": { "type": "string" }
    }
  }
}
```

rachel: LGTM for the JS snippet. The Python part needs an async streaming example for partial JSON accumulation — I'll add that.

jon: Also add a short note about incremental parse strategies and a reference to the SDK helper 'structured_output' so folks don't reimplement fragile parsers. Maybe show a minimal fallback for malformed trailing commas.

maya: Added a quick incremental parse example in the PR to illustrate streaming: ```py
async for chunk in resp.stream():
    buffer += chunk
    try:
        obj = json.loads(buffer)
    except JSONDecodeError:
        continue
    break
```

kevin: Can we also add a tiny unit test to the docs repo to prevent regressions? A snapshot test asserting the example output shape would be ideal.

maya: Yep — I added tests/docs/test_function_examples.py with a basic parse assertion and a snapshot for the returned object. Also fixed two broken links I found (runtime routing page + old tools migration link). Can someone sanity-check the updated URLs?

jon: :eyes: Running linkcheck now.

docs-bot: LinkChecker: 2 broken links found in changed files.

jon: Found the failures — they were the old /runtime/route-guide and /migration/tools links. I updated them to /guides/runtime-routing and /migration/tools-to-functions in the PR.

rachel: Pushed a commit with the async Python snippet included and a small warning about prefix caching causing truncated KV reads in weird workloads. Added a one-line caveat under the performance section.

maya: Great. One last editorial ask from product: can we extract a single-file "quick cheat sheet" example (one request -> one response) for the product-facing examples directory (/examples/quick-function-call.md)? It should be short and copy-pasteable.

sam: Happy to write the quick example tomorrow — can keep it to ~8 lines so it fits in product pages.

maya: Thanks. If there are no objections I'll merge after CI passes and the linkcheck is green. Marking for merge in 2h.

jon: No objections. :shipit:

docs-bot: CI passed — all checks green.

maya: Merged. Will follow up with a tiny follow-up PR to add the quick cheat sheet from @sam. Thanks y'all!
